name: Conservation, Community, and Education Grants
summary: Alberta Conservation Association grants for non-research projects related to wildlife, fish, habitats, conservation education and outdoor activities in Alberta.
reporting: Recipients must provide a progress report by September 1, 2027 and a final report by March 15, 2028.

steps: Email the completed application to ACA

eligibility.rule: Applicants have liability and Workers’ Compensation Board coverage for people involved in the project.
Submit the project to only one ACA-funded grant programme.
Lead is neither ACA staff, a federal or provincial employee, nor a federal or provincial ministry.
All project activities take place from April 1, 2027 through March 31, 2028.
An organisation applying for funding is legally recognised.

reporting.quote: Provide a progress report to ACA by September 1, 2027. The progress report should be in ACA's template, which can be found on ACA's website www.ab-conservation.com b. Provide a final report to ACA by March 15, 2028.

effort.quote: Next opportunity to apply November 1, 2026 - December 10, 2026
Submit your application by e-mailing it to ACA (amy.mackinven@ab-conservation.com) between November 1, 2026 and December 10, 2026 before the deadline Thursday, December 10, 2026, 4:30pm MST.
The Adjudication Committee members assess and rank the grant applications based on the established assessment criteria and funding priorities independently prior to meeting.

eligibility.quote: The organization/individual must have a liability insurance policy and WCB coverage to adequately protect those involved with the funded project.
A project can only apply to one ACA grant program.

with the exception of a federal or provincial government staff and ACA staff. ACA does not fund applications where the federal or provincial government employee is the principal applicant (Principal applicant is considered the lead on a project) or the principal applicant is a federal or provincial ministry.

Research projects (Applications for research projects may go to one of the two ACA grant programs supporting research, either ACA Research Grants or the ACA Grants in Biodiversity for graduate student projects.
Project activities must occur between April 1, 2027 and March 31, 2028.
Any legally recognized organization or individual (with appropriate liability insurance and WCB coverage) can apply if they have a suitable project

after_award.quote: The grants are normally paid in three equal payments. The initial payment is made upon signing the Cooperative Project Agreement, the interim payment is made upon approval of the interim report due Sept. 1st, and the final payment is a hold back paid on approval of the final report due Mar. 15th of the term year and receipt of the signed financial statement.
